title.narrative: SALAR/Avfall Sverige Waste Management for Ukraine (WM4U)

description.narrative: Det övergripande målet för programmet är att förbättra avfallshanteringen i Ukraina i linje med EU:s direktiv och regler, vilket bidrar till att begränsa klimatpåverkan, ökad resurseffektivitet, stärkande av den cirkulära ekonomin, miljömässig hållbarhet och förbättrad livskvalitet för alla. Insatsen implementeras av Sveriges kommuner och regioner under 2024 - 2027.

The overall goal to which the proposed programme will contribute is to improve waste management in Ukraine, with benefits for climate mitigation, resource efficiency, the circular economy, environmental sustainability and quality of life for all. The programme is implemented by the Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions (SALAR) during 2024 - 2027.

The overall goal to which the proposed programme will contribute is to improve waste management in Ukraine, with benefits for climate mitigation, resource efficiency, the circular economy, environmental sustainability and quality of life for all.
This will be achieved by supporting Ukraine to align to EU rules, laws, standards, directives and regulations and by doing so contribute to Ukraine's EU accession process regarding Chapter 27 on Environment and Climate.
The programme is structured around two main areas for support with an expected overall outcome for each:
1. Support for stronger multi-level governance in waste management
Outcome: Improved planning, regulation, financing and coordination between tiers of government with a view to more effective implementation of national legislation and policy on municipal waste management.
2. Support to capacity development in selected municipalities
Outcome: Selected municipalities have strengthened their ability to deliver inclusive and sustainable waste management services.

title.narrative: Beslut om insats SKR/Avfall Sverige kommunal avfallshantering Ukraina

description.narrative:
The first regular narrative report for the Waste Management for Ukraine (WM4U) project will be submitted by 30 April 2026 and the results examples below are from the Brief Programme Update #1 and #2.
Studies, analyses and study visits
Under the outcome on Improved planning, regulation, financing and coordination between tiers of government, the WM4U programme has carried out a number of studies and analyses that contribute to a better understanding of the waste management system in Ukraine and will contribute to improved legislation and policies.
an analysis of the current waste management tariff system in Ukraine completed a comparative study providing an overview of European practices and describing tariff systems in Sweden and Poland in comparison with Ukraine carried out an Extended Landfill Gas (LFG) Study exploring models and systems for the implementation of LFG management measures at selected sites within the Programmes pilot regions
Extended Producers Responsibility (EPR) is one of the programme components and WM4U is organised a high-level study visit to Stockholm on EPR and packaging waste in December 2025. The Ukrainian delegation included representatives from the Parliamentary Committee, the Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture and several city councils. The visit included meetings with relevant Swedish government bodies, industry associations, and producer responsibility organisations.
Established partnerships between Ukrainian and Swedish municipalities
WM4U has successfully selected 4 'pilot clusters' consisting of a number of municipalities around the cities of Ivano-Frankivsk, Vinnytsia, Kremenchuk (Poltava Oblast) and Lozova (Kharkiv Oblast) including collaboration with the Oblast administrations in these regions. The pilot cluster have been paired with Swedish municipal clusters.
Following the visits by the Ukrainian clusters to Sweden and Ukrainian clusters to Ukraine during the first half of 2025 cooperation between the clusters have been established. An important milestone is the completion of four Baseline Reports, which now form the foundation for developing the Local Waste Management Plans (LWMPs) in the respective cluster.
Donations from Swedish municipalities
In total 1617 waste containers and 1 biomethane garbage truck has been donated from Swedish municipalities or municipal waste management companies to Ukrainian municipalities. The donated equipment has been delivered to 4 Ukrainian municipalities namely: Lozova (415 waste containers biomethane garbage truck), Kremenchuk (745 waste containers), Vinnytsia (352 waste containers) och Luka-Meleshkovskaya (105 waste containers).
